NovaBio Therapeutics - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, driven by robust demand for our oncology and immunology franchises, accelerating growth in emerging markets, and the continued effectiveness of our sales and marketing strategies. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including expanding our geographic footprint with a focus on high-growth regions, optimizing our R&D investments across oncology, immunology, and neurodegeneration, enhancing sales force productivity through data-driven tools, analyzing and controlling operating expenses for efficiency, and outlining a clear outlook that positions us for sustained growth.

Our oncology portfolio, particularly OncoTarget, remains a cornerstone, with label expansions driving uptake similar to leading PD-1 inhibitors. In immunology, ImmunoBlock faced some pricing pressures but showed solid volume gains. Emerging markets are emerging as a vital engine, with China and Latin America leading the charge through strategic partnerships and access programs. Our R&D efforts are advancing high-potential assets like next-generation ADCs and gene therapies, while disciplined marketing metrics underscore our commercial prowess. Operating expenses reflect targeted investments yielding pipeline momentum.

We are particularly excited about NovaBispec, our next-gen bispecific antibody, and its potential to capture significant share in solid tumors with improved efficacy and safety profiles.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mike Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Dr. Rivera. As Dr. Rivera mentioned, we had a solid second quarter. Total net product sales reached $2.6 billion, an increase of 12% year-over-year on a reported basis and 14% at constant exchange rates. This increase was primarily driven by strong oncology uptake in the U.S., tender wins in Europe, and explosive growth in emerging markets within our rest-of-world segment.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.20 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $550 million, or $1.50 per share, adjusting for stock-based compensation and one-time items.

Turning to our geographic revenue performance, which really highlights the diversification and resilience of our portfolio across oncology, immunology, and rare diseases. The U.S. accounted for 54% of total revenue, or $1.4 billion, up 7% year-over-year. This was propelled by sustained demand for our flagship PD-1 inhibitor, OncoTarget, which generated $850 million, aided by expansions into MSI-high solid tumors and adjuvant therapies, mirroring the path of products like Keytruda. Immunology sales from ImmunoBlock contributed $350 million, tempered by 3% ASP erosion from PBM rebates by players like Express Scripts and CVS Caremark, with 10% volume growth offset by a slight mix shift to lower-margin hospital products.

Europe made up 26%, or $676 million, flat year-over-year at constant rates due to pricing reforms in Germany via AMNOG and HTA delays in France for NovaBispec, which launched in five major markets this quarter. Biosimilar successes, including our adalimumab equivalent BioHumira, delivered 5% volume gains in Spain and Italy, countering 4% ASP drops from volume-based procurement.

The rest of world, at 20% or $524 million, surged 28% reported and 32% at constant rates, with emerging markets comprising 62% of this segment—about 12% globally—and growing 42%. China led with $205 million, up 55%, fueled by OncoTarget's NRDL inclusion and our WuXi Biologics partnership slashing logistics costs 15% for better tender access, plus post-COVID oncology demand surges. Latin America hit $110 million, up 35%, driven by HepCure's 25% share in Brazil and Mexico via generics ties. India and Southeast Asia added $95 million, up 30%, from RareZyme distribution with Dr. Reddy's and rituximab biosimilars in a booming market. Japan and other developed ROW grew 12% to $114 million on steady reimbursements.

Emerging markets' three-year CAGR of 38% dwarfs U.S. 9% and Europe 4%, thanks to $450 million invested over two years in access programs enrolling 150,000 patients to cut out-of-pocket costs up to 70%, a Hyderabad biologics plant for 2025 approvals, NRDL submissions at 75% success, and localized Phase III trials like our TB vaccine. EM targets 18% of revenue by 2025, 25% by 2027, with $1 billion incremental sales, despite forex hedging at 80% and 40% margins.

Now, on operating expenses, which totaled $452 million, up 19% year-over-year from $380 million, or 68% of revenue on a non-GAAP basis excluding $18 million in stock comp and $12 million restructuring. R&D dominated at $312 million, 69% of OpEx and up 25%, driven by Phase 3 acceleration for BNT-401, our HER2 ADC like Enhertu, with $85 million in recruitment and $45 million milestones. Efficiencies included 15% lower cost per patient via AI matching and 22% savings from Indian CROs; headcount up just 8% to 1,200. SG&A at $128 million, up 7%, reflected sales force adds for oncology and $35 million in marketing/KOLs, with U.S. flat amid IRA, EMEA up 10% on HTAs, Asia down 5%. G&A flat at $12 million via zero-based budgeting and 340B automation.

Drilling deeper into R&D expenses and priorities, we spent $452 million in the quarter, up 14% year-over-year from $397 million and 8% sequentially, pacing toward $1.8-1.9 billion full-year at 37.7% of $1.2 billion core revenue from assets like Zynara. This aligns with Regeneron at 35%, below pure biotechs. Clinical programs took 55% or $249 million for Phase 2/3 derisking, preclinical/platform 25% or $113 million, and manufacturing/regulatory 20% or $90 million. Costs rose 12% from CRO inflation and biologics inputs, with 60% U.S., 20% EMA, 15% China via SinoBioGen.

Investments follow rNPV with >$2B peak and >40% PTCS: Oncology (45%, $203M) leads with NB-ADC-301's $120M Phase 3 ENHANCE-2 for HER2-low cancers (H2 2025 readout, $4.5B rNPV); immunology (25%, $113M) via NB-BI-456 Phase 2b (85% PASI-90); neurodegeneration (20%, $90M) with NB-GT-789 CRISPR for ALS Phase 1/2; platform (10%, $46M) NovaAI cutting timelines 40%. Externalization at 35% saves 15-20%, portfolio pruning freed $75M; expect 32% intensity in 2025.

On marketing and sales effectiveness, our $450 million annual SG&A sees 60% in these areas yielding strong KPIs. For Zepara SGLT2, TRx up 18% to 2.8M, NRx 22% to 1.1M, share 14.2% (16.5% extended). Reps averaged 8.7 calls/day, 78% reach, 22% SOV via NextBestAction AI in Veeva boosting closes 15%. Digital: 4.2M sessions up 42%, ROI 4.8:1 from CTV/social shifts. U.S. 82% revenue with PBM wins; Europe 25% TRx post HFpEF; EM 35% TRx. OncoTarget NRx up 28%, share 9.8%, 92% CLM capture. Ahead: GenAI chatbots, Zepara360 at 78% adherence.

For strategic priorities and outlook, our pillars—pipeline acceleration, commercial excellence, portfolio optimization, global expansion—drive high-teens growth. Pipeline: three BLA filings (NVX-301 PD-1/VEGF 52% ORR, NVX-450 CRISPR sickle cell, NVX-210 anti-TL1A); 14 clinical assets, R&D $2.8-3.0B FY24. Commercial: NVX-101/NVX-150 grew 22%, 87% margins. Optimization: $450M hemophilia sale funds M&A, biosimilars $2B by 2028; OpEx 32-34% margins. Global: U.S. 65%, ex-US 15% growth, Asia milestones $250M, EM 8%. Guidance raised: FY24 revenue $12.5-12.8B (+19%), EPS $6.85-7.05; 2025 18-22% to $15-15.7B, EPS $8.20-8.60, FCF $3.5-4.0B.

Our cash position remains strong at $2.1 billion. For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $12.5 to $12.8 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $6.85 to $7.05.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mike. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, enrollment in the Phase 3 ENHANCE-2 trial for NB-ADC-301 is advancing rapidly across 150 sites, with interim safety data exceeding expectations. NB-BI-456 showed compelling 85% PASI-90 in psoriasis Phase 2b, and NB-GT-789 dosed first ALS patients in Phase 1/2. NovaBispec launched in Europe, with early uptake in five markets. We expect topline readouts for BNT-401 in Q4 and BLA filings for three assets by year-end, plus two approvals in 2025.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Dr. Rivera.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is 1-0-0 to ask a question. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, good morning. Mike, could you expand on the emerging markets growth drivers, particularly the China NRDL strategy and how it factors into your 2025 targets?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, emerging markets were a standout, growing 42% with China up 55% to $205 million on OncoTarget's NRDL inclusion since 2023. Our WuXi partnership cut costs 15%, enabling volume surges amid rising cancer incidence. NRDL submissions for eight assets hit 75% inclusion, better than peers. With access programs, local manufacturing in India, and localized trials, EM hits 18% of revenue by 2025, contributing $1 billion incrementally. Risks like forex are hedged 80%, and we're confident in the trajectory.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. On R&D, how are you prioritizing between oncology ADCs and the higher-risk neuro gene therapy, and any updates on PTCS?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Hi Lisa, great question. Oncology remains 45% of spend with NB-ADC-301 at 55% PTCS and $4.5 billion rNPV, Phase 3 on track for 2025 filing. Neuro like NB-GT-789 is 20% at 35% PTCS but $3.2 billion rNPV upside into Alzheimer's. We're balancing via rNPV framework, pruning low-PTCS assets, and efficiencies like CRO externalization saving 15-20%. Four readouts in 18 months keep us on 15-20% growth path.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel, JPMorgan:
Morning, team. Regarding sales effectiveness, the digital metrics look strong—any color on ROI sustainability amid GLP-1 competition, and SG&A leverage?

Mike Chen, CFO:
Morning, David. Zepara's 4.8:1 ROI held via omnichannel, with 42% digital surge and AI recommendations lifting NRx 22%. OncoTarget share 9.8% with 92% CLM. GLP-1 tailwinds for NVX-150 ramp to $800 million 2025. SG&A at 22% revenue, targeting 200 bps margin gain FY25 via pruning and automation. Biosimilar threats managed, ensuring leverage.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
